name: Quilted cotton armour
description: A sleeveless jacket of raw cotton packed thick between two quilted layers and stiffened with salt, its neck and armholes bound in leather. Very heavy and very hot.
notes: Laid out flat, front up, collar towards +z, 480 mm across, 600 mm long and 40 mm thick: a sleeveless vest with a diamond lattice of khaki quilting over the cream cotton, deep armholes, a neck notch showing the khaki inside, and leather binding round the neck, down both armholes and along the hem. Box/volume x0.8: the padding is laid out flat rather than folded. Slot `torso`, as the gambesons have it: it is meant to be worn as the outer layer by itself. Protection is a judgement for very thick salted padding: strong against blows and cuts, fair against points. The mass follows the reference, which makes it heavier than a gambeson. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Mild steel light chestplate
description: A thin mild steel breastplate and backplate strapped together, with a single lame at the hips and small guards for the shoulders.
notes: Laid out flat, front up, neck towards -z, about 600 mm from the shoulder straps to the fauld and 600 mm across the shoulder guards: a thin breastplate with one fauld lame below it and a single arched lame against each shoulder, a middle ridge and rolled neck and arm edges, the backplate's edge showing round the sides, tan leather shoulder straps buckled on the chest and side straps hanging loose. Box/volume runs x2 to x3.4 and longest x1.14 to x1.22 because the breastplate lies over its backplate with the guards spread beside it, where the reference packs them. Plate in `steel-bright`, the finish for mild steel. Slot `vest`, as the cuirasses and plate suits of earlier armour batches have it, so a padded or cloth `torso` layer goes under it. The reference covers the arms and upper legs too, through the shoulder guards and fauld; Deadvox gives a wearable one slot. Protection is a judgement for mild steel plate. The xl size shares the model. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Bronze bell cuirass
description: An old-style bronze breastplate and backplate, the chest and belly hammered in raised lines and the hem flared out like a bell.
notes: Laid out flat, front up, neck towards -z, 500 mm from the neck to the flared hem and 440 mm across it: a polished bronze breastplate over its duller backplate, raised lines under the chest and down the belly, a rolled rim round the neck and armholes, a flared band at the hem, two pins down each side and tan leather ties over the shoulders. Box/volume x2.9: the backplate fills the breast's curve, so the pair lies as one closed body taller than the packed reference. Slot `vest`, as the cuirasses and plate suits of earlier armour batches have it, so a padded or cloth `torso` layer goes under it. Protection is a judgement for hammered bronze plate.
